interpretations: Group `sentimentandfundamentals` rows by `eventannotm`, with NULL timing as its own group. Compute each group's average `instownpct`, skipping NULL ownership values. "Strictly above average" means the group's average is greater than the overall average `instownpct` across all rows, with NULLs ignored. Output one row with two values: the mean of the qualifying groups' averages, and the mean of how far those groups' averages are above the overall average
Same as 1, but the overall average is the mean of the group averages, meaning each timing group counts equally. This is an average of averages
Same as 1, but the overall average is taken over only the rows with a non-NULL `eventannotm`. The NULL group is still evaluated as a group against that benchmark
Same as 1, but the mean of the qualifying groups' averages is weighted by group row count instead of being a simple mean across groups
Same as 1, but "how far above average" is a percentage or ratio relative to the overall average, rather than an absolute difference in percentage points

Same as 1, but "how far above average" is measured from the overall average of the whole table, and the overall average is computed over rows with non-NULL `instownpct` only. A group whose values are all NULL has a NULL average and is excluded
Same as 1, but the NULL-timing group is treated as a labeled category, such as 'Unknown', and is included in the comparison. If it qualifies, it counts like any other group
Same as 1, but the output is two separate numbers in one row with no rounding, as an unrounded mean of averages and an unrounded mean difference. If no group qualifies, both values are NULL

Same as 1, but the overall average is computed over only rows with a non-NULL `instownpct`, and the "how far above" is measured as the group average minus this benchmark. The NULL-timing group is still included as its own group
Same as 1, but the comparison is made against the overall average of all rows where `instownpct` is treated as 0 when NULL, rather than ignoring NULLs

Same as 1, but "how far above average" is the mean of the row-level differences (each row's `instownpct` minus the overall average) within qualifying groups, not the group average minus the overall average
Same as 1, but the mean of the qualifying groups' averages is computed over the qualifying groups' pooled rows, meaning all rows in those groups are averaged together
Same as 1, but "above average" is judged against the median of `instownpct` instead of the mean
Same as 1, but "strictly above average" means at least one group value exceeds the overall average, not the group average
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT eventannotm, AVG(instownpct) AS a
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals
  GROUP BY eventannotm
),
o AS (
  SELECT AVG(instownpct) AS oa FROM sentimentandfundamentals
)
SELECT AVG(g.a), AVG(g.a - o.oa)
FROM g, o
WHERE g.a > o.oa;
SELECT AVG(avg_cancelpct) AS overall_avg_cancelpct
FROM (
  SELECT ordertimepat, AVG(cancelpct) AS avg_cancelpct
  FROM transactionrecord
  GROUP BY ordertimepat
);
SELECT eventannotm, AVG(infoleaksc) AS avg_infoleaksc
FROM sentimentandfundamentals
GROUP BY eventannotm
HAVING AVG(infoleaksc) > (SELECT AVG(infoleaksc) FROM sentimentandfundamentals WHERE eventannotm IS NOT NULL);
SELECT corpeventprx,
       AVG(instownpct) AS group_avg,
       AVG(instownpct) - (SELECT AVG(instownpct) FROM sentimentandfundamentals WHERE instownpct IS NOT NULL) AS above_overall_avg
FROM sentimentandfundamentals
GROUP BY corpeventprx
HAVING AVG(instownpct) IS NOT NULL
   AND AVG(instownpct) > (SELECT AVG(instownpct) FROM sentimentandfundamentals WHERE instownpct IS NOT NULL);
